404.description: One or both sizes have not been anchored yet.

503.description: Transparency-log store unbound or audit substrate incomplete — retry.

get.description: Apple App-Site Association document fetched by iOS on app install to wire Universal Links into the qub Tauri wrapper (docs/FUTURE.md §16, Phase 2). Routes /auth/verify, /identity/email/change/*, /c/*, /p/*, /u/*, and /s/* into the wrapped app instead of Safari. Returns 404 when APPLE_TEAM_ID or APPLE_BUNDLE_ID is unset in wrangler.toml.

404.description: Wrapper not configured for this environment.

get.summary: Android App Links binding (Digital Asset Links)
get.description: Digital Asset Links statement fetched by Android to verify the qub.social ↔ Android wrapper binding declared in AndroidManifest.xml (docs/FUTURE.md §16, Phase 2 + Phase 8). Once verified, qub.social URLs matching an intent filter route into the wrapped app instead of the browser. Returns 404 when ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME or ANDROID_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 is unset in wrangler.toml (ANDROID_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 is captured at Phase 4 first Play upload).

404.description: Wrapper not configured for this environment.

get.description: Returns the storage block timestamp and intent tag for a sealed qub. No tlock decrypt, no stored-bytes fetch — just a GraphQL lookup with R2 cache. Used by the viewer countdown screen, the `?from={intent}` viral-loop CTA, and the `<qub-embed>` iframe. The qub.social viewer and the embed iframe both re-poll this endpoint every 30 seconds during countdown so the `watching` count climbs live; polling halts in the last minute before unlock. Rate limited 10 requests per minute per IP.

parameters.name: tx_id
parameters.description: Storage transaction ID.

200.description: Metadata. Both fields are optional — empty `{}` means the GraphQL fetch failed or the transaction isn't yet confirmed in a block. Always 200, never 404.

post.summary: Increment the pre-reveal watch counter
post.description: Increments and returns the 'watching' count for a sealed qub. Used by the viewer countdown screen as social proof. No per-fingerprint dedup — accepts ~10% inflation in exchange for a much simpler implementation. Rate limited 10 requests per minute per IP. On rate-limit returns `{ count: 0 }` (200) so the client renders zero or its cached value.

200.description: New count after this increment (or 0 if rate-limited).

post.summary: Commit to watching for a verdict (per-device dedupe)
post.description: Increments the per-qub verdict-watcher set with the caller's device_id. Unlike `/watch`, this counter is per-device-deduped (verdict-uplift-plan §5.1.1): each device counts at most once per qub; re-click is a no-op; unsubscribe does NOT decrement (decoupling subscribed-now from historically-committed defeats hit-and-run gaming). The notify flag that drives verdict-time email fan-out is independent and lives on the `NotifySubscriber` record. Returns the new exact count plus a `watching` flag the client uses to flip the CTA into 'you're already watching' state.

device_id.description: 32-char lowercase hex device identifier. Same `device_id` shape used by /upload and /checkout.

200.description: New count after this commit (rate-limited responses return `{ count: 0, watching: false }`).

watching.description: True iff this device's id is in the set after the call. Used by the client to flip the CTA between 'commit' and 'you're already watching'.

get.description: Returns the current verdict-watcher count without modifying the set. Used by the reveal-page 30-second poll (plan §5.1) so the counter live-updates as new committers tap the CTA.

200.description: Current exact count (cosmetic rounding for display happens client-side).

post.summary: Increment the post-reveal view counter
post.description: Increments and returns the post-reveal view count. Same shape as the watch counter but tracked on a separate KV key. Displayed on the revealed screen as 'Seen by {N} people'. Rate limited 10 requests per minute per IP.

200.description: New count after this increment (or 0 if rate-limited).

post.summary: Subscribe an email to a qub's reveal
post.description: Adds an email address to the notify-me list for a sealed qub. The reveal-time cron sends a one-shot email when the qub unlocks. Always returns `{ ok: true }` on success — re-submitting the same address is idempotent and updates the stored locale. Hard-capped at 1000 subscribers per qub. Rate limited 5 requests per minute per IP.

200.description: Subscribed (or cap reached — the cap is silent so the user doesn't see a degraded experience).

post.summary: Register a Web Push subscription for a qub reveal
post.description: Stores a browser `PushSubscription.toJSON()` payload against the qub. The push-delivery cron sends RFC 8291-encrypted notifications at three cadences (24h / 1h / at-reveal). Idempotent per endpoint URL — re-submitting refreshes the keys and locale. Hard-capped at 500 subscriptions per qub. Rate limited 5 per minute per IP.

endpoint.description: Push service endpoint URL emitted by the browser. MUST be HTTPS AND on the canonical Web Push provider allowlist: `fcm.googleapis.com` (Chrome / Edge / Brave / Opera), `updates.push.services.mozilla.com` (Firefox), or `*.push.apple.com` (Safari 16+). Endpoints on any other host return 400 — added by PR S8 (Andre 2026-05-22 SYSTEMIC-THREAT-REVIEW Finding 58) to close the SSRF-adjacent surface via the delivery cron.

p256dh.description: base64url-encoded 65-byte raw uncompressed P-256 public key (87 chars, no padding).

auth.description: base64url-encoded 16-byte authentication secret (22 chars, no padding).

unlock_at.description: Unlock time in Unix seconds UTC. Used by the delivery cron to schedule cadence dispatch.

locale.description: BCP 47 locale tag for future localised push copy.

400.description: Invalid tx_id, endpoint, keys, or unlock_at.

get.summary: Retrieve the server's VAPID public key
get.description: Returns the base64url-encoded 65-byte raw uncompressed P-256 public key browsers pass to `pushManager.subscribe({ applicationServerKey })`. Cached 1 hour. Returns 503 when the Worker hasn't configured VAPID (staging / local dev).

public_key.description: base64url(65-byte raw uncompressed P-256 public key).

503.description: VAPID not configured on this environment.

post.summary: Issue a magic-link token
post.description: Issues an HMAC-signed, single-use magic-link token for `{ email, device_id }`, stores the token hash in KV with a 15-minute TTL, and dispatches the email via SendGrid. Always returns `{ ok: true }` — the user shouldn't be able to distinguish 'email exists' from 'delivery failed'. Rate limited 3 requests per email per hour. When the email-risk classifier is enabled (`flags:email_risk_classifier_enabled`), addresses on the bundled disposable-domain denylist are rejected with `400 email_not_supported` before any token or send is dispatched. Returns 503 if `AUTH_SECRET` is not configured.

200.description: Token issued and email queued for delivery.

400.description: Invalid email or device_id, or — when the email-risk classifier flag is enabled — `{ error: 'email_not_supported' }` for a disposable-domain hit.

429.description: Rate limited (3 per email per hour).

503.description: Auth not configured (`AUTH_SECRET` missing). Returns `{ code: 'AUTH_DISABLED' }`.

post.summary: Request a six-digit mailbox sign-in code
post.description: Starts the default browser sign-in flow. `device_id` is the browser locator used to scope the short-lived challenge, not account authority. The code expires after 10 minutes and has a five-wrong-attempt budget.

503.description: Auth challenge service unavailable.

post.summary: Verify a mailbox sign-in code and issue the browser session
post.description: Consumes the issuance-bound code, runs the shared identity/account merge, and idempotently issues the host-only HttpOnly browser-session cookie for this exact device. When the device is already linked to another account, the first correct submission returns 409 without consuming the challenge; retry with `account_switch_confirmed: true` only after explicit user confirmation. SessionDO issue is part of the consume fence: unavailability returns 503 and does not fall back to device-link authority.

account_switch_confirmed.description: Explicit user confirmation that this sign-in may replace a different account currently linked to the device. Required when the Worker returns `ACCOUNT_SWITCH_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`.

200.description: Mailbox verified; identity projection returned and `Set-Cookie` issued. The bearer is never present in JSON.

409.description: The device is linked to another account and explicit account-switch confirmation is required. The mailbox challenge remains reusable.

503.description: Identity merge or SessionDO issue unavailable; no browser login authority established.

post.summary: Consume a magic-link token
post.description: With `preflight: true`, validates the capability and reports whether it would switch this device to another account without consuming or mutating anything. Otherwise verifies and consumes the single-use mailbox capability, requires `account_switch_confirmed: true` when replacing another resident account, runs the identity/account merge, and idempotently issues the host-only HttpOnly browser session for the clicking browser's `device_id`. The response JSON contains identity projection only—never the bearer. SessionDO issue failure returns 503 and participates in the un-consume/retry fence.

200.description: Preflight succeeded without mutation, or verification succeeded and `Set-Cookie` establishes the browser session.

400.description: Token failed verification. Returns `{ code: 'TOKEN_EXPIRED' | 'TOKEN_INVALID' }` and the failure reason in `error` (`expired`/`bad_signature`/`malformed`/`bad_payload`).

410.description: Token already used (single-use enforcement). Returns `{ code: 'TOKEN_USED' }`.

409.description: The clicking device is linked to a different account and the request did not include explicit account-switch confirmation. The token remains unconsumed.

503.description: Auth or SessionDO unavailable. No successful identity-only fallback is returned.

post.summary: Request account deletion
post.description: Step 1 of a two-step, proof-of-inbox account-erasure flow. Mints an HMAC-signed token and emails a confirmation link to the address (valid 1 hour); the link opens a read-only HTML page whose button POSTs the actual erase. The confirmation POST must first win an atomic token-hash QuotaDO claim; claim transport failures return a retriable 503 without starting the cascade, and the claim outlives the credential so replay cannot erase a newly recreated account. Always returns 200 — the request response never reveals whether the email has an account. The cascade removes server-side account data (identity, entitlements, payment sidecars, device links, API keys, email→fingerprint reverse-lookup hint, and — since PR S3 / Andre 2026-05-22 SYSTEMIC-THREAT-REVIEW Finding 42 — tombstones the user's handle in the reverse-index so it can't be immediately re-claimed for reclaim-phishing) but cannot remove published qubs from permanent storage, which are immutable by protocol design. Minimised Lightning tax/accounting receipts are retained for at least five years without email, invoice, browser capability, or credentials and are disclosed on the confirmation surface. Rate-limited 3/hour per IP and per email. Returns 503 when `AUTH_SECRET` is missing.

locale.description: Optional BCP 47 locale for the confirmation email.

200.description: Accepted. A confirmation link was emailed if the address has an account.

400.description: Invalid email shape or malformed JSON body.

429.description: Rate-limit exceeded (per IP or per email).

503.description: Auth not configured (`AUTH_SECRET` missing).

get.description: Read-only, prefetch-safe confirmation page. Verifies the one-hour HMAC token and consults the advisory `acctdel-used:<token_hash>` projection so a normally observed spent link renders as expired. GET never claims the token and never mutates account data; POST remains authoritative.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: HMAC-signed account-deletion capability from the confirmation email.

200.description: HTML confirmation form, or the same non-disclosing invalid/expired-link page for an unusable token.

post.summary: Confirm account deletion
post.description: Verifies the emailed capability, atomically claims its namespaced token-hash QuotaDO shard, then runs the idempotent erasure cascade exactly once. A spent/invalid token returns the non-disclosing invalid-link HTML page. The short-lived KV marker is only a GET-page projection; QuotaDO is the single-use authority. A missing or unavailable claim binding fails closed before account state is touched.

t.description: HMAC-signed account-deletion capability from the confirmation email.

200.description: HTML deleted/scheduled page for the winning redemption, or invalid-link HTML for an invalid or already-used token.

503.description: The atomic QuotaDO claim is unavailable. No erasure cascade started; retry the same confirmation form. Includes `Retry-After: 5`.

post.summary: Begin a login-email change
post.description: Requires exact same origin and mailbox proof on the active browser session within the previous 10 minutes. The current account/email/device derive from that principal; caller identity fields are rejected. Validates the new email, creates a 30-minute pending change, and sends verify-new/cancel-old messages. Login email changes only after the new-inbox token verifies.

200.description: Pending record created and both emails dispatched.

400.description: Invalid email shape, same-email request, or — when the email-risk classifier is enabled — `email_not_supported` for a disposable-domain hit on the new address.

409.description: The proposed new email is already registered to a different identity. Returns `{ error: 'email_already_registered' }`. No emails are dispatched in this case.

429.description: Rate-limit exceeded (per old email, per new email, or per IP).

503.description: Session/account or auth service unavailable; no pending mutation created.

post.summary: Complete a login-email change (clicked from the new address)
post.description: Verifies the HMAC-signed token from the email sent to the NEW address, single-use-tombstones it, then runs the atomic identity swap: writes `identity:<new_email>`, re-points every device_link, copies the `verified:<sha256>` record (Sybil counter), deletes `identity:<old_email>` last, and clears the pending record. The order is load-bearing — any partial failure leaves the user reachable on the OLD email. Re-checks identity collision at swap time in case another identity registered while the pending was outstanding.

200.description: Swap completed. The new email is now the canonical login identifier.

400.description: Token failed verification. Returns `{ code: 'TOKEN_EXPIRED' | 'TOKEN_INVALID' }`. Cancel tokens passed here surface as `error: 'wrong_kind'`.

409.description: Identity collision at swap time — the new email got registered while this change was pending. Returns `{ code: 'EMAIL_TAKEN' }`. The pending record is cleared so the user can retry with a different email.

410.description: Token already used (`TOKEN_USED`), pending record gone (`NO_PENDING` — typically because the cancel side won), or OLD identity vanished out-of-band (`IDENTITY_MISSING`).

503.description: Auth not configured (`AUTH_SECRET` missing).

post.summary: Cancel a pending login-email change (clicked from the old address)
post.description: Self-serve recovery primitive — verifies the HMAC-signed cancel token from the email sent to the OLD address, single-use-tombstones it, and deletes the pending record. No login required: the HMAC + nonce + tombstone is the credential. The whole point is enabling cancellation when the user (or rightful holder of the old address) didn't authorise the change.

200.description: Pending change cancelled. The OLD identity is unchanged.

400.description: Token failed verification. Verify tokens passed here surface as `error: 'wrong_kind'`.

410.description: Token already used (`TOKEN_USED`) or pending record already resolved (`NO_PENDING` — typically because the verify side won first).

503.description: Auth not configured.

post.summary: Validate and rotate the browser session
post.description: Exact-same-origin browser endpoint. Validates the HMAC credential against SessionDO and no-ops until it is 24 hours old. When due, atomically rotates one generation, accepts the immediately previous generation for 120 seconds, refreshes the idle deadline up to 30 days, and never advances the mailbox-auth timestamp or 90-day absolute ceiling.

200.description: Session remains active; the current opaque cookie is reminted in `Set-Cookie` and never returned in JSON.

503.description: SessionDO/binding/account authority unavailable; retry without clearing cached identity.

post.summary: Request a mailbox step-up code
post.description: Exact-same-origin endpoint. Email, account, device, and session family derive from the active browser principal; the body cannot select another identity. Reuses the 10-minute/five-attempt mailbox-code primitive.

503.description: Session or challenge service unavailable.

post.summary: Verify step-up and rotate the existing session family
post.description: Verifies the six-digit code against the current account/session/device family, rotates that family, and advances `authenticated_at`. It does not merge/switch accounts, create attestations, resurrect revocation, or extend the original 90-day absolute expiry.

200.description: Recent-auth authority established; replacement cookie issued only in `Set-Cookie`.

503.description: Session/challenge/replay service unavailable.

post.summary: Revoke this browser session and clear its cookie
post.description: Exact-same-origin companion to local-first hard reset. A valid cookie selects the exact SessionDO/device/account; the body cannot choose another caller. The Worker revokes session authority before deleting entitlement/link projections and clears the cookie. Missing/expired authority still clears the cookie idempotently; availability failure is retriable and never falls back to a body device locator.

200.description: Session revoked/pruned or no acceptable cookie was present; cookie cleared idempotently.

503.description: SessionDO unavailable; no account/link mutation performed.

get.description: Resolves immutable account ID and current email from the valid cookie + SessionDO principal. No `device_id`, email, or account query is accepted. Used for boot/visible-tab authoritative revalidation; all responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`. A confirmed 401 clears cached account state, while `SESSION_UNAVAILABLE` tells the client to retain cache and retry.

200.description: Current identity projection for the session account.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked session.

503.description: SessionDO/binding/account index unavailable; fail closed and retain local cache.

get.summary: List browser devices for the session account
get.description: Returns account device locators and a `this_device` flag derived from the session principal. No last-seen/IP metadata or caller device query is exposed.

503.description: Session/account authority unavailable.

post.summary: Revoke one or more account devices
post.description: Ordinary-session incident-response authority; recent step-up is deliberately not required. The body names only the target (`32-hex device_id`, `all_others`, or `all`). For each accepted target the Worker revokes SessionDO first, then entitlement/link/account projections. SessionDO failure stops before later mutation.

200.description: Post-prune device list; `all` also clears the caller cookie.

503.description: Target SessionDO/account authority unavailable; fail closed.

get.summary: Fetch the account's portable signing-key blob
get.description: Returns the cookie-authenticated account's portable signing-key state. The legacy representation uses a nullable blob and reports a missing canonical key as `409 NO_PRIMARY_KEY`; `format=state` returns one of three explicit successful states instead. If `format` is present it must occur exactly once with value `state`. A device locator alone reveals nothing. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Set to `state` to receive a discriminated success union in which `no_primary_key`, `empty`, and `stored` are normal account states.

200.description: Versioned keyblob state for the session account. With `format=state`, this also includes accounts without a canonical key.

account_id.description: Immutable account identifier; the PortableKeyBlob secret-key ciphertext is AEAD-bound to this exact UTF-8 value.

revision.description: CAS token. Zero means no blob exists yet.

blob_b64url.description: base64url-encoded canonical-CBOR PortableKeyBlob, or null before first setup.

400.description: The optional `format` selector was empty, unsupported, or duplicated.

409.description: Without `format=state`, the account does not yet have a canonical signing key (`NO_PRIMARY_KEY`).

503.description: Session/account authority or persisted keyblob state unavailable.

post.summary: Compare-and-swap the account's portable signing-key blob
post.description: Creates or replaces the account-scoped portable signing-key envelope. Requires a valid browser session plus mailbox proof in the previous 10 minutes, then the existing canonical ML-DSA-65 proof and account-scoped Durable Object CAS. Account/device/email derive from the session principal; caller identity fields are rejected. A same-blob lost-response retry is idempotent; stale distinct writes return `409 KEYBLOB_CONFLICT`. No `device_link` or raw-KV fallback is permitted.

blob_b64url.description: Canonical-CBOR PortableKeyBlob encoded as unpadded base64url; 32–16384 bytes decoded; public envelope fields are fully parsed and validated.

pubkey.description: Unpadded-base64url 1,952-byte ML-DSA-65 public key whose SHA3-256 hash is the canonical fingerprint.

signature.description: Unpadded-base64url 3,309-byte ML-DSA-65 signature over the keyblob-store challenge.

200.description: Blob committed, or a same-blob lost-response retry replayed idempotently.

400.description: Malformed JSON/revision/key/signature/timestamp, caller identity field, invalid proof, or malformed/non-canonical blob.

401.description: Session failure or `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` when mailbox proof is older than 10 minutes.

409.description: No canonical signing key (`NO_PRIMARY_KEY`), envelope account/fingerprint mismatch (`ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` / `PRIMARY_MISMATCH`), or stale CAS revision (`KEYBLOB_CONFLICT`, including `current_revision`).

503.description: The required Durable Object CAS binding or storage operation is unavailable; the endpoint fails closed without a raw-KV write.

get.summary: Identity-scoped aggregate of a creator's sealed qubs
get.description: Returns the oldest seal, next reveal, aggregate watchers, and qub count for the browser-session account. Immutable account ID/current email derive from the cookie principal; no device query is accepted. Aggregation is capped at the 200 most recent seals and responses are no-store.

503.description: Session/account authority unavailable.

post.summary: Set the session account's email locale
post.description: Exact-same-origin ordinary-session mutation. Account/email/device derive from the principal; the body contains only a supported BCP 47 locale and cannot select caller identity. Response is no-store.

503.description: Session/account mutation unavailable.

get.description: M2 / DISTRIBUTION-STRATEGY.md §10.1. Computes the p50 and p95 of `shares:<tx_id>` counters across all qubs. Scan is capped at 10k qubs; `truncated` flips when the cap fires.

get.summary: Admin — first-qub to second-qub activation rate
get.description: M8 / DISTRIBUTION-STRATEGY.md §10.3. Walks `identity:<email>` records in the ENTITLEMENTS KV, computes what percentage of new creators seal a second qub within the activation window. Cohort members whose first seal is too fresh to have observed the activation window are excluded so the rate doesn't deflate as the cohort matures.

parameters.name: lookback_days
parameters.description: Cohort lookback window. Default 30, max 365.

parameters.name: activation_window_days
parameters.description: Second-seal deadline measured from the first seal. Default 14, max 90.

get.summary: Admin — qubs below the watcher floor past the seeding window
get.description: M10 / DISTRIBUTION-STRATEGY.md §5.4. Returns qubs whose seal is old enough for the seeding horizon to have elapsed (default ≥48h) but whose watcher count is still below the floor (default <100). Triage list for the growth team. Sorted worst-first and capped at 500 entries.

parameters.name: sealed_after_hours
parameters.description: Minimum age of a qub to be considered 'early seeder'. Default 48, max 336 (14 days).

parameters.name: watching_threshold
parameters.description: Watcher-count floor below which a qub is flagged. Default 100, max 10000.

parameters.name: max_age_days
parameters.description: Ignore qubs older than this. Default 14, max 90.

get.summary: Look up public attestations for a pubkey fingerprint
get.description: Unauthenticated public lookup. Returns the attestation record for a given author-key fingerprint (IDENTITY.md §2 + §4), or 404 if the keypair is unattested (Layer 0). Callers that model Layer 0 as a normal state may set `allow_missing=true` to receive a discriminated `200` result (`found: true` plus the record, or `{ found: false }`). If `allow_missing` is present it must occur exactly once as lowercase `true` or `false`. The viewer uses this at reveal time to render the richest identity label per §5.3. Found records are cached at the edge for 5 minutes; explicit misses are not stored.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: 64-char lower-case hex SHA3-256 of the author public key.

parameters.name: allow_missing
parameters.description: When true, return an explicit successful miss instead of 404 for an unattested fingerprint.

200.description: Attestation record, or a discriminated found/missing result when `allow_missing=true`.

404.description: No attestations for this fingerprint when `allow_missing` is omitted or false (Layer 0 / not attested).

post.summary: Initiate an email attestation challenge
post.description: Issues a 6-digit verification code via SendGrid and stashes a pending challenge in KV with a 10-minute TTL. The submitted public key must hash (SHA3-256) to the claimed fingerprint — this blocks pubkey squatting at the entry point. Rate limited 3/email/hour and 10/IP/hour. When the email-risk classifier is enabled (`flags:email_risk_classifier_enabled`), addresses on the bundled disposable-domain denylist are rejected with `400 email_not_supported` before any code is sent.

400.description: Validation failure. `error` is one of `invalid_fingerprint`, `invalid_email`, `invalid_pubkey`, `unsupported_alg`, `fingerprint_mismatch`, or — when the email-risk classifier flag is on — `email_not_supported` for a disposable-domain hit.

409.description: The fingerprint already has an email attestation. Revoke it first via `DELETE /api/v1/identity/attestation/email`.

post.summary: Complete an email attestation
post.description: Verifies the 6-digit code plus a proof-of-possession ML-DSA-65 signature over the `QUB_IDENTITY_EMAIL_V1` challenge (IDENTITY.md §3.2). Writes the attestation record on success. Attempts are bumped BEFORE the code comparison so brute-force is capped at 5 even on all-fail traffic.

200.description: Attestation written. Returns the full record.

post.summary: Bind this device's signing key to the signed-in email
post.description: Path C (IDENTITY.md §3.2.1). The browser session is the mailbox proof; the caller proves possession of the ML-DSA-65 key with a signature over `"QUB_IDENTITY_SESSION_V1" || fingerprint || i64_be(timestamp) || utf8(session_email)`. Any valid session may link, however old — unless the owner has used the "Not me" link, after which a stale session gets `401 STEP_UP_REQUIRED`. A key already linked to this email returns 200 immediately; otherwise at most 3 new links per account per 24 h, and every new link emails the account a signature-linked alert with a "Not me" link (`unlinkEmailAttestation`). Same-origin only; authority comes from the session, so a body `email` or `device_id` is rejected. Never overwrites a key already attested to a different email.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds; must be within ±120 s of the Worker clock.

signature.description: ML-DSA-65 signature over the challenge, base64url (no padding).

200.description: Attestation written (or already present for this email). Returns the full record.

401.description: No/invalid session (`SESSION_*`), or `STEP_UP_REQUIRED` for a stale session on an account that has used "Not me".

403.description: `forbidden` (not an exact same-origin request) or `fingerprint_blocked` (the owner unlinked this key via "Not me").

409.description: `email_already_attested` (key bound to another email) or `account_changed` (the session's account no longer owns the email).

429.description: `rate_limited` — per-IP limit, or more than 3 new session links for this account in 24 h.

503.description: `service_unavailable` — account lease unavailable, or the signature-linked alert could not be sent (the link was rolled back; retry later).

post.summary: "Not me": unlink a signature from the signature-linked alert
post.description: Redeems the `signature_unlink` capability from a signature-linked alert email (IDENTITY.md §3.2.1). No session and no key signature required — the token was only ever sent to the account email. Unlinks and permanently blocks every signature the reporting browser session linked, clears profile edits made since that session's first link, makes the account's later session links require a recent sign-in, and signs that browser session out. Single-use once complete; a `503` is retryable.

token.description: The `token` query parameter of the alert's "Not me" link.

signed_out.description: The browser session that made the link was signed out.

keys.description: How many signatures that browser session linked, all now unlinked and blocked.

409.description: `account_changed` — the address now belongs to a different account incarnation.

503.description: `AUTH_DISABLED` / `service_unavailable`.

delete.description: Removes the email entry from the attestation record. Requires a proof-of-possession ML-DSA-65 signature over the `QUB_IDENTITY_DELETE_V1` challenge (IDENTITY.md §6.2) — the signature is the auth, no session cookie. When the email was the only entry, the whole record is deleted per §4.2.

400.description: Validation or verification failure. `error` is one of `invalid_fingerprint`, `fingerprint_mismatch`, `timestamp_expired`, `invalid_signature`, `no_attestation`.

404.description: No attestation record exists for this fingerprint.

get.summary: Resolve a qub handle to a representative linked fingerprint and public attestation
get.description: Public reverse lookup. Every email-verified user has a handle (auto-allocated or personalised, IDENTITY.md §3.2.5). The handle belongs to the email-scoped logical identity; this response selects one currently linked fingerprint as a projection locator, not as proof that one keypair owns the handle. Returns 410 with a `released_shape` discriminator while a recently-released handle is still in its cooldown window.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Normalised handle (no leading `@`).

200.description: Handle is claimed; body contains a representative linked fingerprint and the projected public attestation record.

400.description: `invalid_handle` — the handle fails normalisation (charset, length, or reserved).

404.description: Returned in two cases, both with `{ error: "not_found" }`: (a) the handle has never been claimed; or (b) its logical identity has no linked attestation available for public projection (or a legacy fingerprint-owned entry is orphaned).

410.description: Handle was recently released and is in cooldown. `released_shape` is `"auto"` (1h cooldown) or `"user"` (30d cooldown).

post.summary: Change the handle attached to a keypair
post.description: Covers both the first personalisation (rename away from an auto-allocated placeholder) and subsequent renames of a user-chosen handle. A 30-day cooldown applies between renames. Proof-of-possession uses the length-delimited `QUB_IDENTITY_HANDLE_RENAME_V2` challenge (IDENTITY.md §3.2.5). Pre-launch V1 signatures are intentionally invalidated. 503 while the `flags:handle_rename_enabled` flag is off.

200.description: Rename succeeded; body contains the updated attestation record.

404.description: No attestation record exists for this fingerprint.

409.description: `handle_taken` (active claim by another fingerprint) or `handle_in_cooldown` (tombstoned).

503.description: Feature flag off.

delete.description: Tombstones the forward index with a shape-appropriate cooldown (1h for auto-shape handles, 30d for user-chosen) and strips the handle entry from the attestation record. 503 while the `flags:handle_rename_enabled` flag is off.

404.description: No attestation record exists for this fingerprint.

503.description: Feature flag off.

post.summary: Create a Builder API key checkout session
post.description: Creates a Builder Stripe checkout for the immutable account named by a valid browser session with mailbox proof in the previous 10 minutes. Exact same origin is required. Account, device, and canonical email derive only from the principal; caller-selected email/device/account and the retired `device_ticket` are rejected. Turnstile remains an additional bot gate and is checked after session/step-up so a retry does not spend the token. The signed webhook provisions only for the still-existing bound account and cannot establish browser login authority.

turnstile_token.description: Cloudflare Turnstile token obtained from the invisible widget rendered by the developer portal subscribe flow.

locale.description: Buyer's UI locale (BCP 47); stamped onto the Stripe session metadata for post-purchase email language.

400.description: Bad request — missing/malformed Turnstile token or caller identity field.

409.description: The account already has a non-terminal Builder subscription (`already_subscribed`), or another Builder checkout owns the current Stripe idempotency fence (`checkout_in_progress`).

503.description: Session/account authority or checkout configuration unavailable.

post.summary: Capability-bound delivery of a freshly provisioned API key
post.description: After a successful Stripe or Reyls Lightning Builder checkout, durable provisioning AES-256-GCM-wraps the raw API key under a purchase-specific HKDF key and persists an HMAC of the browser retrieval capability. This endpoint requires the matching raw secret before unwrapping (possession of the Stripe session ID or Reyls payment ID alone is insufficient). The first successful delivery opens a five-minute same-capability re-read grace window to survive a dropped response; records then expire. Returns `{ key: null }` while provisioning is pending or after consumption. Because KV can temporarily hide a newly written binding at another edge, a structurally valid browser capability retains its local recovery state and retries an indistinguishable 401 for the bounded 15-minute delivery window; a wrong secret never passes verification once the binding is visible. Rate limited 30 requests per minute per IP.

session_id.description: Stripe checkout session ID. Either this or `invoice_id` is required.

invoice_id.description: Reyls Lightning payment UUID. The legacy 0x-prefixed USDC shape remains accepted only to drain historical purchases. Either this or `session_id` is required.

retrieval_secret.description: 43-char base64url secret issued by the checkout/quote endpoint. Bound server-side to the wrapped key; constant-time-compared before unwrap.

200.description: Key during initial delivery or its five-minute replay window; otherwise null while pending or after expiry.

400.description: Missing or malformed body / session_id / invoice_id.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or wrong retrieval_secret — or no binding record currently visible for the supplied bind key. A browser holding a structurally valid checkout capability retries this indistinguishable response without clearing local recovery state during the bounded delivery window.

405.description: Method not allowed — this endpoint accepts POST only (was GET pre-F-01).

post.summary: Rotate the current API key
post.description: Issues a new API key for the authenticated client and stores a grace-period mapping so the old key continues to work for one hour. Per-period quota state and ownership indexes move forward; `created_at` is preserved. No scope gate — successfully presenting the current key already proves ownership. Concurrent lifecycle mutations are blocked via a two-minute owner-token lease backed by the QuotaDO. `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory. The newly minted secret appears only in the live first response and is never persisted in the replay store. A same-key replay returns 409 with the `ROTATION_REPLAYED` redacted sentinel; use the still-valid old key during its grace window to rotate again with a fresh idempotency key if the first response was lost.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required Stripe-compatible idempotency key. The first response carries the secret; a replay within 24 hours is deliberately redacted and returns 409 `ROTATION_REPLAYED`. MUST match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,255}$`; missing or malformed values return 400.

200.description: Rotation succeeded; the response carries the new raw key.

403.description: Disabled key or IP not allowed. Returns `{ code: 'API_KEY_DISABLED' | 'IP_NOT_ALLOWED' }`.

409.description: A rotation is in progress/committed, or an idempotent replay was redacted as `ROTATION_REPLAYED`.

429.description: Per-account rotation limit exceeded (10 per hour).

503.description: Strong idempotency, quota, account authority, usage migration, or rotation backend unavailable; retry safely with the same idempotency key.

get.summary: List API keys owned by the browser-session account
get.description: Resolves immutable account ID and current email from the valid cookie + SessionDO principal, then walks the account index with legacy email-index reconciliation. Once a record has an account ID, it must match exactly; a stale matching email cannot override another account. No caller device/email query is accepted. The customer-safe projection never includes raw keys, Stripe IDs, or browser credential material; it exposes only a boolean operator lock and actionable disable reason.

503.description: Session/account authority unavailable.

patch.summary: Update label / cap / IP allowlist / scope / disabled on a key the caller owns
patch.description: Partial update requiring a valid browser session, exact same origin, and mailbox proof within the previous 10 minutes. Immutable account ID/current email derive from the principal; caller identity query/body fields are rejected. Once a record has an account ID, it must match exactly; email authority is accepted only for legacy records without one. Unowned hashes return 404 to avoid enumeration.

parameters.name: keyHash
parameters.description: Full SHA-256 hash of the raw key (64 lowercase hex chars). Sourced from the `id` field of `MyApiKeyEntry`.

200.description: Patch applied. Response carries the updated `MyApiKeyEntry`.

400.description: Validation failure, malformed key hash, or rejected caller identity field.

403.description: Exact-origin guard or operator lock rejection.

404.description: The caller doesn't own this key (cross-tenant access) or the key doesn't exist.

503.description: Session/account authority unavailable.

post.summary: Replace a lost or suspected-exposed API key
post.description: Requires an exact-same-origin browser session and mailbox proof within the previous 10 minutes. Ownership derives only from the session principal: immutable account ID must match when present, and email fallback is limited to legacy records without one. Returns a new secret in the live response and immediately revokes the addressed credential with no bearer grace. The dashboard derives its non-secret SHA-256 successor locator locally, renders the vault independently of key-card projection, serialises replacement across every key card until copied-successor confirmation, and preserves confirmed successors against stale multi-key projections; only a successful replacement response with explicit predecessor/successor lineage advances the page-lifetime fence. Durable non-authenticating lifecycle tombstones let a retry reach the live successor after response loss. Billing- or operator-disabled keys cannot be replaced.

parameters.name: keyHash
parameters.description: Full SHA-256 hash from the account-owned key card.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique operation key. A replay is redacted and never returns the replacement secret again.

200.description: Replacement committed; copy the one-response secret now.

403.description: Origin guard or operator lock rejection.

404.description: Key missing or not owned by the account.

409.description: Billing inactive, concurrent mutation, or redacted replay.

503.description: Strong lifecycle backend unavailable; retry.

get.summary: List all API keys with usage stats
get.description: Admin-only listing of every provisioned API key with quota and usage metadata. Used by the admin dashboard for key lifecycle management.

post.summary: Disable, enable, or set the monthly charge cap on an API key
post.description:
Admin-only endpoint that mutates an API key by hash. Three actions are supported:

- `disable` — flip the `disabled` flag to `true` so the key is rejected on every subsequent request.
- `enable` — flip the `disabled` flag to `false`.
- `cap` — set (or clear) the optional `max_monthly_charge_usd` cap on a Builder key. The request body must be `{ "max_monthly_charge_usd": number | null }`. When set to a positive number, the seal + read paths reject with 402 `MONTHLY_CAP_REACHED` once the projected end-of-period overage charge would exceed the cap. Setting `null` removes the cap. Opt-in by design — the cap is the customer's own configured limit, sidestepping EU P2B Reg 2019/1150 unilateral-restriction obligations.

parameters.name: key_hash
parameters.description: SHA-256 hash of the API key (as returned by `GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys`).

requestBody.description: Required only for `action=cap`. Body shape: `{ "max_monthly_charge_usd": number | null }`. Ignored for `disable` / `enable`.

200.description: Action applied; returns the updated key state.

400.description: Missing key hash or invalid action.

404.description: API key not found.

get.description: Content-negotiated viewer entry point. For browsers: serves the SPA index.html. For bots (Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, Slackbot, Discordbot, etc.): returns edge-computed HTML with OG meta tags built from the sealed qub's unlock time and live watch count. For requests with `Accept: application/json`: 307 redirects to `/api/v1/qub/{tx_id}`.

parameters.name: tx_id
parameters.description: Storage transaction ID.

200.description: HTML — either the SPA shell (browser) or bot meta tags.

307.description: JSON-accepting clients are redirected to the JSON read endpoint.

get.description: Public loader script — alias for the current pinned version. Publishers `<script async src="...">` this on their page; the script registers the `<qub-embed>` custom element. Served with `text/javascript`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=86400`, and public CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`).

503.description: Embed bundle not deployed (no `embed/v1/loader-current.js` object in R2).

get.description: Pinned v1 loader URL — same content as `/embed.js` for the lifetime of v1. Publishers should use this in production for stability: it gives a versioned URL that won't break when the loader is updated. Served with `text/javascript`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=86400`, and public CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`).

503.description: Embed bundle not deployed (no `embed/v1/loader-current.js` object in R2).

get.description: Bundled iframe app (~73 KB gzipped) — runs inside the iframe shell, performs in-browser tlock decrypt and renders the qub. During countdown it re-polls `/api/v1/qub/{tx_id}/meta` every 30 seconds so the watching count climbs live (matching the qub.social viewer); polling halts in the last minute before unlock to avoid racing the reveal transition. Served with `text/javascript`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=86400`, and public CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`).

503.description: Embed bundle not deployed (no `embed/v1/loader-current.js` object in R2).

get.description: HTML shell loaded inside the `<qub-embed>` iframe. Carries a locked-down CSP and intentionally OMITS `X-Frame-Options` so it can be embedded on third-party pages. Ships an inline first-paint skeleton (centred qub wordmark + pulsing lime dot, honouring `prefers-reduced-motion`) so the reader sees a branded placeholder while the iframe-app bundle parses; the skeleton is replaced by the first `render()` call from the bundle. The bundle also sets `<title>` dynamically once the qub's intent is known (e.g. `Sealed prediction · qub.social`) so direct-iframe visits get a useful tab label; terminal states (loading / denylisted / unsupported / error) keep the bare `qub` title so the page never claims `Sealed prediction` on a removed or broken qub. Accepts an optional `lang` query parameter (BCP 47 tag); when present it is written onto `<html lang>` and passed to the iframe-app, which resolves it against the locale registry via the same candidate chain used by server-side email templates. Unknown tags fall back to English. Served with `text/html; charset=utf-8` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`. Full publisher-facing contract in `docs/EMBED.md`.

parameters.name: tx_id
parameters.description: Storage transaction ID.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: BCP 47 locale tag (e.g. `en`, `fr`, `pt-BR`, `en-GB`). Loose shape gate at the Worker boundary — the iframe-app re-coerces and walks the candidate chain. Absent or malformed → defaults to `en`.

404.description: Invalid tx_id.

get.description: Returns the raw stored artifact for a qub: private OuterWrapper CBOR or public bare SealedQubCbor. Uses R2 cache-aside and immutable caching (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`). The in-browser embed and SPA resolve the delivery shape, then perform client-side tlock decryption without redundant storage-gateway hits. Rate limited to 120 requests per minute per IP — higher than the JSON `/api/v1/qub/{tx_id}` endpoint because each viewer/embed page-load typically issues one bytes request to refresh the cache.

200.description: Raw stored artifact bytes: private OuterWrapper CBOR or public bare SealedQubCbor.

404.description: qub not found in permanent storage.

get.description: Returns the canonical-CBOR inclusion proof for an anchored qub (PROTOCOL.md §16.9): the exact leaf bytes, the leaf index, the anchored tree size, the RFC 6962 audit path, the committed Merkle root, and the AnchorRef (the Arweave anchor that committed that root). A standalone verifier (`tools/qub-verify --anchor`) recomputes the leaf hash, folds the audit path, and checks the result against the anchor — it never trusts a supplied hash. Proofs resolve from the permanent R2 substrate plus the anchor, so reclaiming LogDO storage never invalidates one. Cached `public, max-age=3600`.

parameters.name: tx_id
parameters.description: Arweave transaction id (base64url, 1-64 chars, at least 8 distinct characters).

200.description: Canonical-CBOR InclusionProof (leaf, index, size, audit path, committed root, AnchorRef).

404.description: Unknown tx_id, insufficient entropy, or the qub is not yet anchored.

503.description: Transparency-log store unbound, or the store advanced past the anchored size mid-window — retry.

post.summary: Record a reaction on a revealed qub
post.description: Records a `called_it` or `wrong` reaction for a revealed prediction and returns the updated tallies. Client-side dedup via localStorage per (tx_id, device) is assumed; ~10% inflation is acceptable. Rate-limited 10/min/IP as a shallow abuse floor — over-limit requests return current tallies without mutating.

post.summary: Stage a signed pact envelope for co-signing
post.description: Browser ceremony that stages a signed pact envelope. `device_id` remains a quota locator. A valid matching browser session may select the account quota/index branch; no cookie stays anonymous and never follows `device_link`. Presented bad/unavailable session authority fails closed and a mismatch returns `SESSION_DEVICE_MISMATCH`. A valid `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory so an ambiguous response cannot charge or create a second staging artifact; missing keys return `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`. Turnstile, signature proof, recipient send budget, and the seven-day stage lifetime remain independent controls. API-key bearer authentication is not accepted.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required stable operation key for the signed staging mutation. MUST match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,255}$`.

envelope_cbor.description: Base64-encoded canonical CBOR QubEnvelope with content_type=0x03, sig_alg=0x01, author_pubkey and author_signature present, cosigner fields absent.

locale.description: Optional BCP 47 locale used for the review invite email.

email_sent.description: Whether the invite email to Party B was accepted for delivery.

email_skipped_reason.description: Why no invite was sent when `email_sent` is false; `null` when it was sent. `unverified_author`: the signing key carries no email attestation matching the browser session — attest it (`attestEmailViaSession`) and call `sendPactInvite`.

get.description: Returns the staged pact's CBOR envelope fields, decoded PactTerms, and Party A's public key so Party B can review before co-signing. If the pact has already been co-signed, returns a sealed redirect payload with `tx_id` and `delivery_url`. While awaiting co-signature the payload also carries `invite_emailed` (boolean): whether the invite email to Party B has been accepted for delivery. The sealed payload carries `unlock_at` (Unix seconds, or null once the staging object has aged out): a pact co-signed inside its unlock buffer is sealed but not yet openable, and clients should hold until then rather than forward to the viewer countdown.

404.description: Staging id not found or expired.

delete.summary: Retract a staged pact before co-signing
delete.description: Party A proves possession of the author signing key and retracts a pending staged pact. Requires a fresh retract signature over `SHA3-256("QUB_PACT_RETRACT_V1" || staging_id_bytes)`.

retract_signature.description: Base64 retract signature from Party A's signing key.

404.description: Staging id not found or already sealed.

post.summary: Email Party B the invite for a staged pact
post.description: Author-only recovery for a stage whose invite was skipped (`email_skipped_reason`). Same eligibility as stage: the pact's author key must carry an email attestation equal to the browser-session email, the pact must be structured (`pact_schema = structured/v1`) with a Party B contact, and it must still be awaiting co-signature. Idempotent once an invite has been accepted for delivery. Send attempts are capped per pact and share the per-recipient daily budget with stage.

parameters.name: staging_id
parameters.description: Staging id returned by `POST /api/v1/pact/stage`.

200.description: Invite accepted for delivery (`already_sent: true` when an earlier send had succeeded and nothing was re-sent).

403.description: `forbidden` (not same-origin) or `author_unverified` (the pact's signing key is not attested to this session's email).

404.description: `staging_not_found` / `staging_expired`.

409.description: `custom_pact` or `missing_contact` — the signed terms cannot be emailed.

429.description: `rate_limited` (per-IP limit, per-pact attempt cap, or another send for this pact in flight within the last 60 s) or `recipient_rate_limited`.

502.description: `email_send_failed` — the provider refused the send; retry later.

503.description: `QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE`.

get.description: Unix seconds by the Worker's clock, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Clients that commit to a near-future instant the Worker will judge (a pact's `unlock_at`) measure their clock offset with this.

post.summary: Co-sign and publish a staged pact
post.description: Browser ceremony in which Party B submits their ML-DSA-65 cosigner signature over the same `sig_input` as Party A. The worker merges both signatures into the envelope, seals with tlock, durably stores the artifact, and schedules permanent-storage publication. Pact publication does not currently append to the transparency log. If Party B's contact in the staged pact is an email, the cosigner is gated by a short-lived 15-minute email-verification marker produced by `/api/v1/auth/verify` (protocol spec §9.7). When the magic-link request that produced the marker carried a `cosigner_fingerprint` (PC-3 binding), the submitted `cosigner_pubkey` must hash (SHA3-256) to the same fingerprint — otherwise the cosign is rejected. Turnstile is required; API-key bearer authentication is not accepted.

400.description: Invalid signature, pubkey, or email-binding marker missing.

404.description: Staging id not found or expired.

409.description: Pact is already cosigned (`already_cosigned`) or another cosign is in progress (`cosign_in_progress`). Retry of the in-progress case is safe once the prior request completes.

post.summary: One-click accept of a pact invite from the email link
post.description: Consumes the single-use emailed pact capability and writes a short-lived, pact-scoped cosign marker. Invite acceptance does not sign the browser into the invite address, issue a browser session, mutate an identity, or create an attestation. An optional cosigner fingerprint preserves PC-3 key binding.

staging_id.description: Staging ID from the URL path.

token.description: HMAC-signed invite token from the `?t=` query param of the email link. Format: `base64url(payload).base64url(sig)`.

cosigner_fingerprint.description: Optional — SHA3-256 fingerprint of the keypair Party B will cosign with. When present, the Worker pins the marker to this fingerprint so a different keypair cannot later cosign (PC-3 binding).

200.description: Pact-scoped cosign marker committed. No account session or identity mutation is performed.

400.description: Invalid token (`TOKEN_INVALID`), expired (`TOKEN_EXPIRED`), staging_id mismatch, malformed body, or invalid fingerprint.

404.description: The staging record was retracted or has expired.

409.description: Pact has already been cosigned (`already_sealed`).

503.description: Auth/token authority unavailable (`AUTH_DISABLED` or `service_unavailable`).

get.summary: Cross-device pact list for the browser-session account
get.description: Derives immutable account ID and current email from the cookie principal, then returns the account/email pact indexes for folder hydration. No caller `device_id` query is accepted; a copied locator reveals nothing. Responses are no-store.

unlock_at.description: Unix seconds when the pact body becomes decryptable (mirrors `envelope.unlock_at`). Optional — entries written before this field was added omit it; clients should default missing values to 0.

503.description: Session/account authority unavailable.

get.description: Resolves a 7-character base62 short code allocated at upload or seal time to the canonical `/c/{tx_id}` viewer page via HTTP 302. Preferred over `/c/{tx_id}` for tweet text and QR matrices because it saves ~56 characters.

404.description: Unknown short code.

get.description: oEmbed 1.0 discovery endpoint for public qubs. Returns a JSON oEmbed payload whose `<qub-embed src=...>` uses the fragment-less public viewer URL, so WordPress, Notion, Medium, and Substack can auto-embed without a manual snippet. Private delivery requires the complete secret-bearing URL and should use the explicit publisher snippet instead; this endpoint never reflects a wrapper key.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Canonical qub viewer URL (e.g. `https://qub.social/c/<tx_id>`).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response format. Only `json` is supported.

404.description: URL does not match a known qub.

get.description: Dynamic OG card for a qub. Sealed state renders intent + reveal date + watching count; revealed state renders intent + called-it percentage as a results card. R2 cache-aside by state + watching/reaction bucket so unfurls hit cache for the typical viewer flow. Note: despite the `.png` URL suffix (kept for compatibility with OG cards already in the wild), the response body is **SVG** (`Content-Type: image/svg+xml`). Major social-media unfurlers (X, Discord, Slack, Reddit, Threads, Bluesky) accept SVG.

404.description: Unknown tx_id.

get.description: One-click unsubscribe endpoint linked from creator lifecycle emails (seal confirmation, pre-reveal, post-reveal, anniversary). The `token` query parameter is HMAC-signed and binds the request to a specific email + scope (per-qub for the first four; identity-wide for the anniversary scope). On success, writes a suppression record so subsequent lifecycle sends to that address skip delivery. **Always returns 200 with a confirmation HTML page**, even on token failure (expired, malformed, replayed) — surfacing a 400 to a user clicking from their inbox is a worse UX than silently no-op'ing, and any leaked information would help an attacker probe token validity. Token failures are logged operator-side.

200.description: Unsubscribe confirmation HTML page (always returned, regardless of token validity).
